description:
Project: Mixed-workload scheduler prototype (Serving Runtime Performance: Kernel + Scheduling).

Goal
- Reduce user-visible p95 tail latency for text generation under mixed prompt-length distributions (short chat prompts interleaved with long-context prompts) without materially regressing throughput or fairness.

Problem framing
- Redwood’s continuous batching and KV-cache-heavy decode path performs well in steady-state homogeneous workloads, but mixed workloads can cause head-of-line blocking where long-prefill or long-context requests dominate GPU scheduling and queue selection, inflating p95.
- The prototype introduces a short/long prompt-aware policy (two-queue or class-based scheduling) to bias service toward latency-sensitive short prompts while still guaranteeing progress for long prompts.

Scope
- Runtime scheduler changes: request classification, queueing, dispatch policy, and guardrails (aging, starvation prevention, max skew, burst caps).
- Kernel/runtime interactions: prefill vs decode separation, token budgeting, and ensuring kernel selection doesn’t thrash when mixing sequence lengths.
- Observability: new scheduler metrics/traces (queue depth by class, time-in-queue, prefill latency, per-class p50/p95, starvation counters).
- Benchmarking and evaluation: synthetic mixes (e.g., 80/20 short/long), replay of anonymized production traces, and perf-canary integration.
- Rollout: feature flag + config knobs; staged canary in one region and a subset of Dedicated pools; rollback plan.

Out of scope (for prototype phase)
- Full multi-tenant QoS productization (customer-configurable classes/tiers beyond internal knobs).
- Large-scale admission control redesign (only minimal coupling to existing backpressure).

Stakeholders and roles
- Eng Serving Runtime (Scheduling): Sofia Ivanova (EM), Lena Fischer (tech lead), Marcus Reed, Omar El‑Sayed, Julian Moore.
- Eng Serving Runtime (Kernels): Hiro Tanaka (EM), Grace Kim, Yuki Sato.
- SRE/Observability: Sean Gallagher, Allison Grant, Rafael Mendes, Aisha Bello.
- Product alignment: Nikhil Sharma (Hosted API), Lauren Bishop (Dedicated), Paula Mendes (rollout telemetry requirements).

Timeline and milestones (hypothetical)
- Phase 0 (1–2 wks): workload analysis + design review + ADR.
- Phase 1 (2–4 wks): implement scheduler prototype behind flag + instrumentation + unit/regression tests.
- Phase 2 (2–3 wks): benchmark suite + perf-canary + iterate on policy parameters.
- Phase 3 (1–2 wks): limited production canary + SLO monitoring + decision to graduate/iterate.

Key deliverables
- Confluence design + ADRs; benchmark methodology + results; runbook/rollout plan.
- Linear initiative with tracked tasks and dependencies.
- GitHub PR series implementing the prototype and follow-up fixes.
- Slack coordination threads across runtime, SRE, and releases.
- (Optional) customer-facing escalations captured via Jira + sales/CS artifacts when the work is triggered by real customer pain.

files.description: Primary design doc: problem statement, proposed short/long classification, scheduling algorithm (two-queue / class-based), starvation prevention, config knobs, and rollout plan. Includes diagrams of prefill/decode pipeline and queue interactions.

ADR capturing the decision to implement short/long prompt-aware scheduling (vs alternatives like pure SRPT, strict token-based fairness, or admission-control-only). Documents trade-offs, risks, and success criteria.

Benchmark plan: workload mixes, datasets/prompts, model set, hardware SKUs, regions, run protocol, warmup, and reporting. Defines metrics (p50/p95, throughput, TTFT, queue time) and pass/fail thresholds.
Results write-up for the prototype on runtime-1.18 candidate: tables/graphs, deltas vs baseline, notable regressions, and recommended default parameters per SKU.
Profiling playbook update: how to reproduce contention, what traces/metrics to inspect, Nsight/Triton profiling tips, and common failure modes (kernel thrash, cache eviction spikes).
Dashboard spec for per-class scheduler metrics (queue depth, waiting time, starvation counters) and alert thresholds aligned to SLO/error-budget policy.
SRE doc defining SLO guardrails for tail latency during canary: allowed p95/p99 drift, rollback triggers, and error-budget considerations for regions/pools.
Operational runbook: enabling the feature flag, safe parameter ramps, monitoring checklist, known-bad signals, and rollback procedure. Includes owner rotation and escalation steps.
Known issues/edge cases: pathological mixes, starvation corner cases, interactions with KV cache compaction, and hardware-specific anomalies.
Kickoff notes and early brainstorming: goals, non-goals, open questions, rough algorithm ideas, and who owns each workstream (scheduling, kernels, SRE).
Working spreadsheet (represented as a table) summarizing prompt-length distributions from anonymized traces, candidate thresholds for short/long, and sensitivity analysis.
Informal doc capturing simulation outputs (queueing model assumptions, SRPT vs two-queue), plus notes on what matched/didn’t match production behavior.
Raw benchmark capture: run logs, parameter sweeps, tables for p50/p95/throughput across mixes/SKUs, and links to Grafana/perf-canary runs.
Draft canary plan: target pools, ramp schedule, success metrics, owner on-call coverage, and rollback criteria (pre-Confluence version).
Team retro notes: what went well, what surprised us (e.g., kernel selection instability), and follow-ups for productization.
PR adding request classification (short vs long) based on prompt/context length and/or predicted prefill cost; includes config flags and unit tests.
Core PR implementing two-queue (short/long) dispatch policy with aging/starvation prevention, plus basic correctness tests and perf notes.
PR refactoring scheduler hooks to better separate prefill and decode scheduling decisions and avoid long-prefill dominating batch selection.
PR enforcing per-iteration token budgets per class to limit tail amplification; adds counters and debug logs for budget overruns.
PR adding metrics/tracing: per-class queue depth, time-in-queue, starvation counter, dispatch share, and p95 by class; includes dashboard stubs/metric docs.
Benchmark-lab PR adding standardized mixed workload scenarios (80/20, 50/50, long-spike) and report generation for p95 deltas.
Perf-canary PR introducing a job that runs mixed workload tests nightly on representative SKUs/regions and alerts on regressions.
Follow-up bugfix PR addressing an edge case where long requests could starve under sustained short traffic; adjusts aging function and adds regression test.
PR wiring config knobs through runtime config system (per pool / per model defaults), with validation and safe bounds.
PR updating internal runtime metrics documentation with links/IDs for new scheduler dashboards and how to interpret them during incidents.
Top-level Linear initiative/epic: scope, success metrics (p95 reduction targets), timeline, and sub-issues for implementation, benchmarking, and rollout.
Task to pull anonymized distribution stats, define short/long threshold candidates, and publish a brief summary to Drive/Confluence.
Design review ticket: schedule review, gather feedback from kernels + SRE, track approval items, and link to Confluence design/ADR.
Implementation task for classification logic and config wiring; includes acceptance tests and rollout gating.
Core scheduling task: implement two-queue dispatch, fairness/aging, and add simulation-based checks if available.
Instrumentation task defining metric names, labels, and dashboard requirements; partner with Observability (Allison Grant).
Benchmark suite task: add workloads, automate reporting, and define comparison baselines for p95 and throughput.
Perf-canary integration: schedule nightly jobs, set alert thresholds, and route notifications to #eng-runtime and #eng-sre.
SRE review ticket: rollback triggers, error budget policy, and monitoring checklist before enabling in production.
Release planning ticket for canary enablement: target pools, feature flag strategy, comms, and follow-up decision meeting.
PM ticket aligning success criteria (Hosted vs Dedicated), acceptable throughput trade-offs, and how results will be communicated internally.
Thread in #eng-runtime coordinating kickoff: proposed thresholds for short/long, links to trace analysis, and owners for design/benchmarks.
Thread in #eng-runtime debating policy details: two-queue vs SRPT approximation, starvation prevention, and interaction with continuous batching.
Thread in #architecture reviewing ADR: concerns about fairness, multi-tenant implications, and what must be gated behind config/feature flags.
Thread in #eng-runtime during implementation: questions about prefill/decode separation, code pointers, and quick perf sanity checks.
Thread in #eng-runtime reporting an edge case (long queue starving) found in load tests; includes logs/snippets and proposed fix.
Thread in #eng-sre defining dashboards/alerts for new scheduler metrics and agreeing on rollback triggers for canary.
Thread in #eng-releases coordinating canary rollout steps, feature flag changes, and who is on point during the ramp window.
Thread in #incidents about a brief p95 spike during early canary; triage notes, mitigation (rollback vs parameter tweak), and follow-up action items.
Customer support ticket for a Dedicated account reporting p95 spikes during mixed short/long prompts; includes environment details, investigation notes, and links to runtime canary results.
Customer support ticket alleging TTFT/p95 regression when long-context traffic increases; includes reproduction steps, Grafana links, and recommendation to test scheduler prototype.

Fireflies transcript: SE-led technical deep dive with an enterprise prospect about tail latency under mixed workloads; captures requirements, success criteria, and agreement to run a benchmark with proposed scheduling changes.
Email thread seeking exec/SRE approval to enable the scheduler prototype in a limited prod canary; includes risk assessment, rollback plan, and links to dashboards/bench results.

HubSpot company record for a prospect with strict tail-latency requirements; includes notes referencing mixed-workload pain, linked Fireflies technical deep dive, and next steps for benchmark validation.
